notes: Klemera-Doubal parameters from published age curves. Each biomarker follows x(a) = mean25 + slope (a - 25) + accel max(0, a - knee)^2 with residual SD `sd` given age. Shapes (slope, knee, accel) come from the cited studies. Levels (mean25, sd) are set for a fingertip reach in a headset, which none of the studies used, so they are provisional until re-anchored on a young-adult group on the device. Refit on collected sessions and bump `version`.

catch_latency.source: Simple-RT shape, little slowing before ~50: Der and Deary 2006, Psychol Aging 21(1), UK HALS n=7130. Baseline from ruler-drop RT, Eckner et al. 2010; device level not calibrated.

reach_rt.source: Simple RT nearly flat until ~50 then accelerates: Der and Deary 2006; young-adult minimum, rise through adulthood: Dykiert et al. 2012, n=1994.

rt_tau.source: RT variability higher in older adults after controlling for speed: Hultsch, MacDonald and Dixon 2002 (extreme groups, slope not sourced); ex-Gaussian tau rises with age: West et al. 2002.

choice_rt.source: Choice RT slows across adulthood: Der and Deary 2006. Keypress go RT 277 ms at ~18 to 351 ms at 60-69 (Communications Medicine 2025, s43856-025-01239-1), scaled by ~1.5x for reach; UK Biobank ~3 ms/yr at 40-70 (npj Aging 2021, s41514-021-00067-6).

omission_rate.source: Go/no-go omissions 1.09% (~18), 3.06% (60-69), 4.92% (70-79), 10.05% (80+): Communications Medicine 2025. Curve fit to those group means. That study used a 500 ms deadline; Gate's 2 s window will give fewer omissions, so sd is set wide.

corsi_span.source: Span SD 1.03 and r(age) = -0.46 over ages 21-89, implying about -0.025 span/yr: Facchin et al. 2024, PMC11554723. Young-adult level 6-7 depends on protocol: Kessels et al. 2000; Pagulayan et al. 2006.

pursuit_rms_cm.source: Direction only: older adults track with larger error and lag (Neuroscience 2026, S0306452226004264; 3D tracking, T&F 2024, 18824889.2024.2359183). Magnitude is a placeholder with a deliberately shallow slope so it carries little weight until fitted.
